title: Defence SMEs need banking services that work
summary: The UK's most innovative businesses often start small.Before they can develop new technologies, win contracts or expand into new markets, they need access to banking services to help them operate, invest and grow.Access to financial services can be easy to take for granted. When those services work well they're almost invisible. However, when access becomes difficult or delayed, the effects can extend far beyond a single business.Small-to-medium sized enterprises (SMEs) operating in or providing services to the defence sector play an important role in innovation and growth.But these businesses do more than contribute to economic growth. Many are helping to develop the technologies, expertise and capabilities that support the UK's national resilience and security.Banking services are part of that story. They help businesses secure contracts, invest in new opportunities and grow. title: Chandler King (City) Limited enters creditors’ voluntary liquidation
summary: On 17 September 2026, Chandler King (City) Limited (Chandler King) went into creditors’ voluntary liquidation. Grace Jones and Karyn Jones of Parker Andrews were appointed as joint liquidators. Chandler King, an FCA-authorised firm, was an independent financial adviser which advised on investments and pensions. On 28 April 2026, Chandler King agreed to a voluntary requirement with the FCA, which restricted its activities. Before entering liquidation, Chandler King applied to cancel its FCA permissions, which is subject to review by the FCA.
